# Spring Boot host config. H2 in-memory in the same JVM; Flyway migrates the schema up on boot from
# db/migration; Actuator health is the readiness probe.

# In-memory H2 (dies with the JVM = clean per-run reset). A change waits up to 10s on rows an as-of view
# holds (see SheetPasts).
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:officehq;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1;LOCK_TIMEOUT=10000
spring.datasource.driver-class-name=org.h2.Driver
spring.datasource.username=sa
spring.datasource.password=
# Pooled connections are never retired: when HikariCP closes one at its default 30 min
# max-lifetime, this in-memory H2 closes under the remaining sessions and every later statement
# fails with "The database has been closed" while the health probe stays UP. 0 means no lifetime.
spring.datasource.hikari.max-lifetime=0

# Flyway owns the schema. JPA does not create tables.
spring.flyway.enabled=true
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=none
# Close the persistence context at the end of the request, not during view rendering.
spring.jpa.open-in-view=false

# Readiness probe.
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health
management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true

# The SPA is served from src/main/resources/static (built there by bin/build); deep-link
# fallback is in SpaConfig.java.

# Audit sink: one record per line to this known file, so tests assert side-effects by reading it.
# bin/start passes an absolute path via AUDIT_FILE; default is .run/audit.log.
app.audit.file=${AUDIT_FILE:.run/audit.log}

Each pool member's line now shows their cut for every period that ended on or before the sheet's today, as the cut stood at the end of that period. The cell is empty when the member had no cut then. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests, twice in a row, and the server log shows no errors or deadlocks.

**How it works:** the app already saves a copy of the whole sheet each time its today moves on (`SheetPasts`), which is how the existing "as of a date" view works. For each period that has ended, the server loads the copy from the period's last day and works out the pools from it in a transaction that is always rolled back. That gives the pool, its members, the pot and the holds as they were then. A period ending exactly on today uses the live sheet.

- **Server:**
  - `Pools.java`: a new `history(sheetId)` returns the pools for each ended period.
  - `PoolController.java`: each member in the pools response now carries a `periodCuts` list of `{period, cut}`. Nothing in the stored data changed, so there is no migration.
- **Front end:** `pools.ts` shows a `pool-cut-<period name>` cell on each member's line, one per ended period.

**One change outside the pools code you should know about:** the first full run failed because closing a period deadlocked against a pools reload that was building one of these past views. I changed `SheetPasts.java` so a past view locks the sheet's row first, the same way changes already do. A change in progress is now waited for (up to the existing 10-second lock timeout) instead of deadlocking. This also affects the existing as-of view.

**Cost to watch:** every pools load now rebuilds the sheet once per ended period. That is quick with the test data, but a sheet with many ended periods will be slower to load. If that matters, the past results could be cached, since a saved copy of the sheet never changes.
